written.myAnswer: A strong acid ionizes extensively in water; a concentrated acid contains a large amount of acid per given volume of solution.
An Arrhenius acid produces H⁺ (or H₃O⁺) ions in water. An Arrhenius base produces OH⁻ ions in water.
Hydrochloric acid in the stomach helps digest food. Excess stomach acid can cause acidity, which can be treated with antacids such as magnesium hydroxide that neutralize the excess acid.
